question: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ -3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}$. If $AB$ is a symmetric matrix, find the relation between $a, b, c, d$.
explanation:
Let $AB = P = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ -3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}$

$= \begin{bmatrix} 2a+3c & 2b+3d \\ -3a+4c & -3b+4d \end{bmatrix}$

$P$ is symmetric $\implies P' = P$

So: $2a+3c = 2a+3c$ (ok)

$-3a+4c = 2b+3d$

$2b+3d = -3a+4c$ (Repeat)

$-3b+4d = -3b+4d$ (ok)

Thus, $2b + 3d = -3a + 4c$.

Final answer: $2b + 3d = -3a + 4c$.
